summary.headline: MapmyIndia Q4 FY26: revenue up 54.8% QoQ, EBITDA margin 44.6% (+460 bps YoY), but FY26 revenue only INR474 crore vs INR463 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported a sharp sequential Q4 recovery: revenue up 54.8% QoQ, EBITDA up 141% QoQ, PAT up 171% QoQ, with EBITDA margin at 44.6% and PAT margin at 31.3%. Full-year FY26 growth was muted, with revenue moving from INR463 crore to INR474 crore, as government contracts were delayed or deferred into FY27. Management attributed the Q4 shortfall against its own expectations (about INR45-50 crore by an analyst's estimate) to customer-side delays of roughly INR20 crore in an automotive IoT order plus government push-outs, all described as timing rather than lost business. Management reiterated the INR1,000 crore FY28 roadmap and an order book of about INR1,750 crore, but gave no formal FY27 growth guidance.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR463 crore in FY25 (c.1-2% growth)

financial_highlights.value: INR3.50 per share (175% on INR2 face value)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR133 crore in March 2025 (per analyst)

segments.name: A&M (Automotive & Mobility)
segments.commentary: Grew about 9% for FY26 per management. Q4 automotive core business described as soft by an analyst; management said a Hyundai-related variation was a drag, while attach rates and program presence rose YoY.

segments.name: C&E (Consumer & Enterprise, incl. Government)
segments.commentary: Declined about 3% for FY26, which management attributed to government contracts delayed into FY27. C&E rose 142% QoQ in Q4. Government open order book closed above INR200 crore; government billing crossed INR100 crore and cash collection crossed INR100 crore in FY26.

segments.name: IoT-led business
segments.commentary: Management said IoT EBITDA margin rose from 14% in FY25 to 16% in FY26, with Q4 margin at about 33%. Management called this a quarterly high driven by operating leverage and a better SaaS mix, not a one-off.

segments.name: Mappls App
segments.commentary: Cumulative downloads above 45 million, with 10+ million added during FY26. Amazon Now was cited as a corporate API/SDK integration example, with rollout in Bengaluru and Mumbai.

guidance_outlook: Management is confident of growth 'above 20%' in FY27 per the 5-year trajectory, and an analyst asked whether 25% growth is achievable; management said there was 'no reason not to believe' 25% growth is possible but gave no formal number.
INR1,000 crore revenue roadmap for FY28 is unchanged; timing is under review year by year.
Open order book about INR1,750 crore (including 18% GST); billing about INR520 crore and sales about INR470 crore in the order book breakup.
Management expects the INR20 crore IoT order delayed in Q4 to reflect in Q1 and Q2 FY27, and government push-outs to Q1-Q2 FY27.
Management plans to change segment reporting from FY27 Q1 to Auto & Retail, Corporate and Government, with restated FY26 quarterly figures.
Management targets IoT EBITDA margin above 16% in FY27 and sees steady-state IoT margins above 16%.
capex_capacity: Capital allocation in FY26 was about INR120 crore for organic growth (government, IoT, intellectual property); small acquisitions were minor.
IoT hardware is capitalised as fixed assets and depreciated over 3 years under the opex subscription model, so IoT growth needs capital.

Inventory of IoT devices rose to support expected demand; management said purchases are based on portfolio forecasts, not specific orders, and that hardware price inflation is being offset through pricing and value engineering.
Government business requires working capital, mainly receivables, to fund delayed payments at Mappls DT and Gtropy.
No specific capex amount for FY27 was given.
demand_pricing: FY26 open order book began at about INR1,500 crore; about 18% (c.INR270 crore) converted to revenue, and INR780 crore of in-year new orders produced about INR200 crore of in-year revenue (about 25%).
Management said the FY26 conversion rate could be 'higher' in FY27, but gave no number.

Fixed-price contracts are used in government (milestone-based), corporate (lump-sum or minimum guarantee) and IoT (fixed fleet size or minimum guarantee, 3-5 year SaaS terms). Management described fixed-price visibility as 'very clear', with volume contracts historically flexing up.

Government receivables: management said there have been almost no bad debts in government, but collection periods are longer. Trade receivables rose from INR133 crore to INR176 crore YoY (per analyst), against flat revenue.
Management said a government 'Large Energy response system' order and a large government IoT tender (re-tendered) were delayed, outside its control.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there a weak full-year performance in automotive/mobility and consumer-enterprise, and what is the FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said total FY26 revenue was INR474 crore vs INR463 crore; C&E fell about 3% because government work was delayed and A&M grew about 9%. Q4 C&E rose 142% QoQ. The government order book is above INR200 crore, and management is confident of significant growth in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order book to revenue conversion outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 conversion was about 18% of the INR1,500 crore opening book. Management declined to give a fixed range but said FY27 could be higher.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital allocation plan for the roughly INR600 crore cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Organic growth comes first (IoT, government, IP). IoT hardware is capitalised and depreciated over 3 years, and government needs working capital. No acquisition, dividend or buyback plan was detailed beyond the FY26 final dividend.

qa_highlights.question: Where was the Q4 revenue shortfall of about INR45-50 crore vs expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a roughly INR20 crore automotive IoT order delayed by customer regulatory requirements (now fulfilled, expected in Q1-Q2), a government Large Energy Response order delayed by the government, and a large government IoT tender sent to re-tender. Management called these push-outs, not lost business.

qa_highlights.question: Why is core C&E flat, and will the segment reporting change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the corporate API/SDK revenue ramps with usage (Amazon Now cited), with a gestation period. Segment reporting will move to Auto & Retail, Corporate and Government from Q1 FY27 with restated quarterly FY26 figures.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables rise and is there a collection concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said government receivables reflect a longer collection cycle with no material bad debt; Mappls DT collected prior-year receivables, with overdue amounts expected to be lower than total receivables. DSO was described as better than industry.

qa_highlights.question: Why did IoT margins rise to about 33% in Q4 and is inventory a factor?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the margin to operating leverage, better mix (more SaaS) and cost optimisation, and denied inventory gains. Inventory rose to meet expected IoT demand. Management targets IoT EBITDA margin above 16% in FY27.

risks_watch: Execution timing: revenue conversion is lumpy and dependent on customer readiness and government approvals; Q4 slippage of about INR45-50 crore by analyst estimate.
Receivables: trade receivables rose about 32% YoY to INR176 crore against flat revenue; watch DSO and government collections in Q1 FY27.
IoT input cost inflation (DRAM/NAND prices cited by an analyst) versus rising IoT margins; watch whether margins hold and whether inventory-linked gains recur.
Geopolitical and government budget pressure cited by an analyst; management said it saw no change to business as usual.
Revenue CAGR of 1-2% in FY26 versus the 25-30% growth an analyst asked about; watch Q1 FY27 for conversion to a FY27 growth rate and the FY28 INR1,000 crore target.
Segment reporting change from Q1 FY27 will affect comparability.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident and upbeat about the Q4 inflection and FY27 pipeline, but became defensive and less specific when pressed on the FY26 shortfall, the revenue gap, and receivables. It gave no quantified FY27 guidance and declined to name accounts or quantify the delayed government orders.
key_quotes: Q4 marked a positive inflection point with improving business activity and stronger execution.
So our road map continues with INR1,000 crores. The team, the entire leadership team is working on it.
The gap is maybe 5 accounts or 6 accounts, but the orders exist.
Our first priority, which we believe is the right way to do is to provide organic growth.

growth.why: Management is confident of growth above 20%, with 25% possible but not formally quantified, backed by an open government and corporate order book of about INR1,750 crore; FY26 revenue grew only about 1-2% to INR474 crore, and the Q4 rebound is partly timing-driven, with the FY28 INR1,000 crore roadmap kept but timing open.
